 Switzerland v Scotland LIVE: Scots target Nations League promotion as Andy Robertson makes history
 Robertson has broken Sir Kenny Dalglish’s appearance record and wins 103rd cap against the Swiss
 Jamie Braidwood Monday 16 November 2026 14:59 EST

 It is set to be a historic evening for Andy Robertson in Switzerland ( PA ) There’s plenty at stake for Scotland as they take on Switzerland in their Nations League finale as a hopes of gaining promotion to the top-tier are still alive. A 2-1 win over North Macedonia affords Sebastien Pocognoli’s side an opportunity to clinch second place in Group B1 but they must win at the Sitterstadion in St Gallen tonight.
 Switzerland have already secured top spot in the group and Scotland must take three points from tonight’s contest and hope that Slovenia fail to beat North Macedonia in the other group clash in Skopje. There is also a knock-on effect for Euro 2028, with second in the Nations League likely to hand the Tartan Army an easier qualifying group, despite being a co-host, with a pot two seeding before the draw.
 It is also a historic night for captain Andy Robertson who has become Scotland's most-capped male player in history, beating Sir Kenny Dalglish’s record of 102 appearances, after leading out the team this evening. 
 Follow the Nations League clash between Switzerland and Scotland, below:

 Scotland XI: Gunn; Hickey, Porteous, Graham, Tierney, Robertson; Ferguson, Gilmour; McGinn, McTominay; McBurnie 
 Switzerland 0-0 Scotland
 9 mins: That’s another smart move from Scotland, well worked through midfield, finding the gaps in Switzerland. It’s then played first-time around the corner towards McTominay, but he’d gone too soon and was caught offside. 
 Encouraging signs from Scotland, though. 
 Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:58 Switzerland 0-0 Scotland
 7 mins: McGinn is slightly late on Schmidt after a fast Swiss break down the left. It’s a poor free-kick from the left and Ferguson heads it away. 
 Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:56 Switzerland 0-0 Scotland
 6 mins: A chance for Robertson to swing the ball into the box from the set-piece. The cross has got a lovely shape on it, but Switzerland clear and then deal with the second phase as well as Robertson’s right-footed cross was blocked. 
 Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:55 Switzerland 0-0 Scotland
 3 mins: A lovely move! A flick from McGinn finds McBurnie, who plays it on to the advancing Hickey. The right back has options to his left, including Robertson, but is quickly swallowed up. That was well designed from Scotland, though. 
 Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:52 Switzerland 0-0 Scotland
 2 mins: The Swiss forward Ballet looks to use his twinkle toes as he wins an early corner. From the rebound, Schmidt takes aim from range but Gunn collects easily enough. 
 Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:50 KICK-OFF! Switzerland 0-0 Scotland
 1 min: We’re underway in St Gallen, and Skopje. 
 Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:49 Switzerland v Scotland
 A cracking Flower of Scotland warms up a chilly evening in St Gallen in the east of Switzerland. 
 Kick-off is next. 
 Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:44 Switzerland v Scotland
 Andy Robertson is wearing a special pair of boots to mark his record 103rd Scotland cap, with light blue tongue. 
 He leads his team-mates out against this much-changed Switzerland side knowing victory is needed to have any chance of keeping their hopes of promotion alive. 
 We’ll be keeping an eye on Skopje, too, as a North Macedonia point against Slovenia is needed as well.

 Switzerland XI: Mvogo; Comert, Elvedi, Bajrami, Athekame; Freuler, Jashari, Schmidt; Sanches, Botelli, Ballet
 Substitutes: Kobel, Keller, Britschgi, Nyakossi, Zakaria, Embolo, Amdouni, Rodriguez, Sow, Itten, Aebischer, Rieder. 
 Scotland XI: Gunn; Porteous, Graham, Tierney; Hickey, Ferguson, Gilmour, Robertson; McGinn, McTominay; McBurnie.
 Substitutes: McCracken, Bain, Adams, Christie, Hendry, Penrice, McPake, Curtis, Gannon-Doak, Bowie, Patterson, Montgomery. 
 Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on BBC Scotland, BBC Two and BBC iPlayer 
 ( PA ) Jamie Braidwood 16 November 2026 19:42 Sebastien Pocognoli praises Andy Robertson ahead of historic 103rd Scotland cap
 "I just told him that he has to enjoy it and after it's just a bonus for the future,” Pocognoli said when asked about Robertson becoming Scotland’s all-time record men’s appearance holder. 
 "So he needs to enjoy, to play with freedom. He has a lot of experience, so I don't need to tell him, but again, we are really proud of what we are living together with him. And the best way to have a good feeling for him is to have a good game."
